chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyād, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I asked him about a man who forgot the ẓuhr until the time of ʿaṣr entered. He said: He begins with the ẓuhr. Likewise with the prayers, one begins with the one that was forgotten, unless you fear that the time of the prayer will go out; then you begin with the one whose time you are presently in, then make up the one you forgot.

key_terms.تَقْضِي: you make up a missed prayer after its time
key_terms.وَقْتُ: the legally designated time of a prayer

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets ẓuhr until the time of ʿaṣr begins, which salat (prayer) should be performed first?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the order of performing missed obligatory salat (prayer) when the time of another obligatory salat (prayer) has already entered. The principle is to begin with the missed prayer first, unless doing so would cause the current prayer time to expire, in which case the current prayer is performed first and the missed one is made up afterward.
